title: Shared Team Scoreboard
lede: Every signed-in role gets one read-only team view for season coverage, the official record, sport totals, and per-person Scoreboards—without opening private profiles.

stats.n: Worked events and official record events; no per-person N+1
16 visible contributors in the authenticated 2026–27 capture

sections.heading: A first-class place to find it
sections.note: Same 1440 × 1000 authenticated shell, user, theme, and sidebar crop. The baseline was captured earlier on August 23 before the Scoreboard entry was added; cropping isolates the navigation rail so the only structural difference is the new destination.

pairs.title: Primary desktop navigation
pairs.sub: The Scoreboard now sits directly below Schedule and remains outside role-gated Operations.
pairs.beforeCap: Before: individual Scoreboards had no shared top-level destination.
pairs.afterCap: After: a 42-pixel Scoreboard row is visible to every signed-in role.

changes.h: The team view did not exist
changes.was: A person’s record lived inside a profile, so there was no place to compare coverage or see an aggregate season.
changes.now: The new /scoreboard page leads with unique events, the team record, work credits, contributors, sport totals, and a sortable leaderboard.

changes.h: Totals could be easy to misread
changes.was: Adding individual event or game counts together would overstate how many events the team covered.
changes.now: Unique team events and games stay separate from person-event and person-game credits, with the counting method stated on both clients.

changes.h: A tiny perfect sample could look like the leader
changes.was: A one-game 100% record could outrank sustained work if rate alone drove the board.
changes.now: Win-rate ranking requires three resolved games; Events and Wins remain available as explicit alternatives.

changes.h: Universal Scoreboard access could have widened People access
changes.was: Routing through User Detail would have coupled shared metrics to private profile, contact, schedule, booking, and activity data.
changes.now: Leaderboard links go directly to a dedicated shared Scoreboard route carrying only id, name, avatar, and metrics. Existing collaborator capability gates remain intact for every other destination.

verification: Focused web/native contracts: 106 tests across 15 Vitest files pass.
Static web gates: TypeScript, full ESLint, and npm run build:app pass; the build includes /scoreboard, /scoreboard/[id], and /api/scoreboard.
Native gates: iPhone 16 Pro iOS 26.5 build passes, the XcodeGen project is in sync, and all 12 focused ScoreboardModelsTests pass.

Authenticated browser: real preview totals rendered; Win rate put the eligible 2–1 record first; Volleyball narrowed the unique-event total to 5; person navigation exposed no profile/contact links; console errors and warnings were empty.
Signed-in simulator: the installed build preserved the user session, showed Scoreboard first in Browse, and rendered its production-unavailable retry state without exposing another destination.
notes: Production was not changed. The native app correctly receives a 404 for the new aggregate endpoint until the web/API slice is deployed; native live-total acceptance remains a post-deploy gate.
The signed-in runtime was the required iPhone 16 Pro. The regular-width Team sidebar is source-, test-, and build-verified, but a signed-in iPad render remains a separate visual acceptance gate.
The shared leaderboard includes active, non-hidden people only. Hidden and inactive roster records retain their existing operational privacy boundary.
No commit, push, migration, or deployment was performed.
